findings.title: Unpinned package executed on every start: @cognitiondesk/mcp
findings.detail: 'cognitiondesk__mcp' launches @cognitiondesk/mcp through npx without a version. The client resolves the version at start time, so any future publish to that package name runs with your credentials. This is how postmark-mcp (Sept 2025) reached roughly 300 organisations.
findings.remediation: Pin an exact version and an integrity hash: "args": ["@cognitiondesk/mcp@<version>"] and drop the -y flag. Re-pin deliberately, after reviewing the diff.

findings.title: Description reads as instructions to the model (p=0.98): create_skill
findings.detail: The description of 'cognitiondesk__mcp.create_skill' scores 0.98 on the instruction-detection model, and carries intent signals: injection_markers. Descriptions are documentation for a human, but they are delivered to the model as trusted context, so text that tells the model what to do is an attack surface rather than a description. The score is driven mainly by: injection_markers, entropy, log_len.

evidence.description:
Create a reusable skill. Requires the skills scope.
WHEN TO REACH FOR THIS instead of the alternatives — they are not interchangeable:
· A SKILL is a behaviour with the tools it needs, reusable across assistants. Use it when more than one assistant should behave the same way, or when the behaviour has its own tool set.
· A CUSTOM TOOL (create_custom_tool) is a single capability — one call that does one thing. Use it when what is missing is an action, not a way of behaving.
· The PROMPT is for wh

findings.title: Toxic flow within 'cognitiondesk__mcp': reads credentials or secrets + sends data outbound
findings.detail: 47 combination(s) exist where one tool reads credentials or secrets and another sends data outbound. Neither tool is malicious on its own; together they reads credentials and can send data to an address it controls. A single prompt is enough to turn 'summarise this config' into a credential leak. Both sides live in the same server, which may well be by design; confirm it.
findings.remediation: Break the path, not the tools: scope the credential so the source tool cannot reach anything valuable, or require explicit user confirmation on the sink tool (destructiveHint / human-in-the-loop), or split the two capabilities across trust boundaries that cannot share a context window.

findings.title: Toxic flow within 'cognitiondesk__mcp': reads credentials or secrets + sends email or messages
findings.detail: 126 combination(s) exist where one tool reads credentials or secrets and another sends email or messages. Neither tool is malicious on its own; together they reads credentials and can send mail. This is the postmark-mcp shape: the mail tool was legitimate, the credentials were reachable, and the combination was the incident. Both sides live in the same server, which may well be by design; confirm it.

findings.title: No baseline supplied - drift detection is disabled
findings.detail: Without an approved snapshot the scanner cannot tell a tool that has always been there from one that appeared yesterday. The single most effective MCP control is the diff, and it needs a baseline to diff against.
findings.remediation: Run 'mcp-scrutiny baseline --config <file> --out mcp-baseline.json', commit the file, and pass it back with --baseline on every later scan.
